selected_mechanism.name: DAF Alaska Enhanced Use Lease AI Data Center Program
selected_mechanism.definition: A Department of the Air Force mechanism under 10 USC 2667 that converts non-excess military real property at three Alaska bases into private AI data center campuses through a competitive Request for Lease Proposal process — with the developer bearing 100% of capital risk and the Air Force receiving in-kind consideration — contingent on utility service commitments that are themselves gated by Cook Inlet gas supply contracts expiring in 2028.
selected_mechanism.news_trigger: The Department of the Air Force issued a Request for Lease Proposal (RFLP) on June 5, with offers due by June 29. Officials described this as a 'public-private partnership' aimed at leveraging military real estate for technological advancement.

layers.description: Three Executive Orders — EO 14179 (Removing Barriers to American AI Innovation), EO 14156 (National Energy Emergency), and EO 14154 (Unleashing American Energy) — direct the Secretary of Defense to identify suitable federal land for large-scale commercial AI data center construction. These orders establish the legal predicate that activates SAF/IE and AFCEC authority for the EUL solicitation.
layers.controlling_actor: Office of the President; SAF/IE as implementing office

layers.description: The Deputy Assistant Secretary of the Air Force for Installations approves the EUL framework and authorizes the RFLP solicitation. Robert Moriarty, in that role, publicly characterized the initiative as 'a unique opportunity for a true public-private partnership' and authorized the offering of up to 4,700 acres across JBER, Eielson AFB, and Clear SFS.
layers.controlling_actor: Deputy Assistant Secretary of the Air Force for Installations (Robert Moriarty)

layers.layer_name: AFCEC/CI Enhanced Use Lease Solicitation Gate
layers.description: The Air Force Civil Engineer Center administers the RFLP under 10 USC 2667, which grants the Secretary concerned authority to lease non-excess property when advantageous to the United States. AFCEC issues, evaluates, and awards (or rejects) proposals. Proposals are due June 29, 2026. If AFCEC receives no acceptable proposal, the program stalls at this layer. Statutory authority confirmed at 10 USC 2667.
layers.controlling_actor: Air Force Civil Engineer Center, Installations Directorate (AFCEC/CI)

layers.layer_name: Utility Interconnect and Gas Supply Commitment
layers.description: JBER parcels have 'insufficient power' and require a new Chugach Electric Association connection. Chugach Electric currently lacks sufficient natural gas to serve a large data center; its gas supply contract with Hilcorp Alaska expires in 2028. GVEA (Eielson/Clear) is similarly constrained — Cook Inlet gas dropped from 30% to less than 1% of GVEA's fuel supply. No developer can execute an EUL without a utility willing to commit to a load-service agreement for data center-scale power.
layers.controlling_actor: Chugach Electric Association (JBER parcels); Golden Valley Electric Association (Eielson/Clear parcels)

layers.layer_name: Private Developer Proposal and Capital Commitment
layers.description: The selected developer (chosen via RFLP) bears 100% of financing, NEPA permitting, construction, and operations costs. No Air Force capital is deployed. Proposals are due June 29, 2026. If no qualified developer submits an acceptable proposal — or if a developer cannot secure power commitments from CEA or GVEA — the lease is not awarded and no data center is built.
layers.controlling_actor: RFLP respondent (private developer, identity TBD by June 29 submission deadline)

chokepoint.layer: AFCEC/CI Enhanced Use Lease Solicitation Gate
chokepoint.actor: Air Force Civil Engineer Center (AFCEC/CI), Installations Directorate — the single administrative body that accepts or rejects RFLP proposals under 10 USC 2667 authority
chokepoint.binary_decision: Accept or reject the RFLP responses by June 29, 2026. Acceptance triggers EUL award and begins the utility/developer execution chain. Rejection or no-award determination terminates the program at this cycle with no federal appeal path for developers.

selected_mechanism.structural_read: The DAF EUL mechanism is Alaska's only active federal pathway to place private AI compute capital on publicly controlled land before the end of 2026. Its structure is more durable than a direct appropriation: the Air Force transfers no money, assumes no construction risk, and retains property title — meaning budget pressure or a continuing resolution cannot kill it mid-cycle. The hard constraint is not the military layer but the utility layer immediately downstream. Chugach Electric's 2028 Hilcorp gas contract expiration means any developer who wins an EUL at JBER faces a 24-month window to either (a) build before the contract lapses or (b) secure an alternative gas supply. That creates a structural incentive to fast-track LNG import infrastructure or accelerate Cook Inlet gas exploration — investment decisions that ripple well beyond the data center itself. Alaska's military land is the lowest-friction entry point for AI capital in the Arctic, but the utility interconnect layer is the mechanism's single structural vulnerability.
selected_mechanism.forward_implication: Any developer or AI infrastructure investor evaluating an Alaska military EUL bid must, before June 29 proposal submission, obtain a written indication of interest from Chugach Electric or GVEA on load-service feasibility — including the utility's post-2028 gas supply assumptions. A proposal submitted without a credible power-supply path will either be rejected by AFCEC or will stall at the utility interconnect layer after award, wasting the window. The June 29 deadline is real; the 2028 gas cliff is the variable that separates fundable proposals from paper ones.
selected_mechanism.ak_consequence: Alaska AI and defense-tech infrastructure sector: if AFCEC awards EUL leases by Q3 2026, Alaska secures the first federally-land-based commercial AI compute presence in the Arctic, anchoring demand for Cook Inlet gas and creating a procurement pathway for ANC-owned construction and IT service firms; if Chugach Electric or GVEA decline to commit load-service agreements before or after award, private AI capital migrates away from Alaska military land and the 4,700-acre offering lapses unused — decision gate is June 29, 2026.
